correctness_confidence.basis: Theorem structure and proof logic sound given external dependencies. Lemma 2 (Tang et al.) and Fang [4, Theorem 3] from September-October 2026 preprints: if erroneous, all results fail. Numerical verification: Theorem 4 tested on 16000 instances to 5.0×10⁻¹⁶ precision; Proposition 12 relies on numerical rather than closed-form computation. No errors detected in accessible parts, but reverse parameter closure (equation 20) and some key identities lack detailed algebraic verification.

rigor.basis: Proofs are detailed with explicit boundary case handling. Paper marks external dependencies and non-new results. Assumptions stated precisely. However: (1) Lemma 2 proofs not independently verified despite being critical, (2) Section 7 depends on Fang [4] convexity proof 'not formally verified here', (3) Proposition 12 uses numerical rather than closed-form derivatives, (4) floating-point verification acknowledged as 'error-finding aids, not proofs'. Rigorous within scope but dependent on unverified external work.

novelty.basis: Main novelty is extension from boundary λ²=k (covered by Tang et al., OpenAI, and concurrent Fang [4]) to interior 0≤λ²<k using three-vertex geometry. Genuine but incremental. Complementary channel results (Theorems 9-10) somewhat novel but straightforward given the additivity result. Section 7 extends Fang's techniques using Araki-Lieb-Thirring—solid but not groundbreaking. Paper explicitly disclaims new Davies dynamics, minimum-entropy optimization, or convex roof geometry.

significance.basis: Determines exact Davies channel capacities, extending additivity from boundary λ²=k to interior 0≤λ²<k. Provides complementary channel simulation and entanglement cost formulas; proves Rényi multiplicativity and strong-converse exponents. Limited scope: specialized to one family, no practical applications, original simulation and quantum capacity remain open. Primarily of interest to quantum information theory community. Solid incremental advance but not field-changing.

reproducibility.basis: Supplementary Python scripts with NumPy, SciPy, mpmath provided. Verification runs documented (21 October 2026 for v2, 25 October 2026 for v3). Explicit output comparisons: Theorem 4 tested on 16000 random instances, capacity hull evaluations match text to 3.8×10⁻⁶ bits, complementary properties verified to ≤5.0×10⁻¹⁶. However: floating-point only (not interval-certified), scripts acknowledged as 'error-finding aids not universal proofs', and high-precision verification relies on 75-digit mpmath rather than closed forms. Good support but limitations acknowledged.

summary: This manuscript extends classical capacity results for qubit Davies channels from the boundary λ²=k to the interior region 0≤λ²<k using a novel three-vertex block entropy decomposition. Main contributions: (1) Theorem 1 establishes capacity additivity χ(Φ⊗N)=χ(Φ)+χ(N) for arbitrary partners in the full Davies region; (2) Theorems 9-10 determine exact complementary channel capacity and parallel simulation cost; (3) Section 7 proves Rényi multiplicativity and exact strong-converse exponent. Work is mathematically sound, well-documented, and includes numerical verification. Critical results depend on Lemma 2 (Tang et al. [2]) and Fang [4, Theorem 3], both September-October 2026 preprints not yet peer-reviewed. Contribution is incremental (extends boundary techniques to interior) and specialized (quantum information theory). Some proofs rely on numerical verification rather than closed forms (Proposition 12). Transparent about scope limitations. (Original assessment: 4 stars from 4.5 score; overall_stars=5 is schema rounding only.)

Proposition 12 strict inequality J'(1/2)=(1/10)ln(2639/77)>0 relies on numerical verification rather than explicit algebraic derivation

potential_errors: Lemma 2 (triangular entropy inequality): If this foundational result from [2] contains an error, all downstream theorems fail catastrophically. Status: external dependency from preprint
Fang [4] convexity argument for norm compression: Paper acknowledges 'appendix convexity proof is not formally verified here'. If error in [4], Section 7 results invalid

Proposition 12 derivative: J'(1/2) calculation involves cancellation of logarithmic terms. Numerical verification to 10^(-170) given but algebraic path not fully shown. Risk: high-precision floating point error

Reverse parameter closure (equation 20): The constraint 1-a_p-b_p=k_p verified in text through substitution at q=t, but general algebraic identity not fully expanded. Supplement has numerical checks only
Formula (8) entropy inequality: Boundary cases (u=0, vanishing row masses) are handled, but edge case where row masses vanish and K=0 simultaneously should be checked

Convex envelope computation (10): Claimed that minimum integral over probability measures with mean p is achieved at most two support points. This uses compactness; verify measure space assumptions hold
strong_novelty_candidates: Three-vertex block entropy decomposition (Theorem 4) using controlled purifications at third vertex - genuinely extends two-vertex boundary results with new technique
Exact parallel simulation cost formula (19) for complementary channel with explicitly computed reversed parameters - determines previously open quantity for full Davies family
Corollary 11 elementary closed form in convexity region - provides rare closed-form capacity formula in specific parameter regime
State entanglement cost strong additivity on Davies Stinespring range (Corollary 7) - new application of additivity to constrained bipartite states

Fang [4] convexity proof not independently verified for Section 7. Paper states 'appendix convexity proof is not formally verified here'. Recommendation: Independently verify or mark Section 7 as dependent on unreviewed external convexity argument.
